tagline: From the clothespin town up into the spruce.
intro: Out of Richwood, 2,325 feet up at the forks of the Cherry River, WV 39 follows the North Fork east into the Monongahela National Forest to the Cranberry Mountain visitor center. There the parkway begins. WV 150 runs along the ridges of the Allegheny Front, with dark spruce on the high ground and four overlooks, crosses Black Mountain at 4,550 feet and comes down to US 219 north of Marlinton.
The parkway was dedicated in 1980 and is left alone in winter. It is not plowed, and in those months it is the one place in the forest where snowmobiles may run.

moments.title: Richwood
moments.text: A coal and lumber boom town that once had the world's largest clothespin factory, and every April holds a festival as the Ramp Capital of the World.

moments.title: Cranberry Glades
moments.text: Five peat bogs at 3,400 feet that resemble Canada's, the southernmost home of many of their plants, from cranberries to the carnivorous pitcher plant and sundew.

moments.title: Big Spruce Overlook
moments.text: A boardwalk here tells how careless logging and the fire after it left Black Mountain bare for decades. The mountain is the highest point on the road.

practical: WV 150 is not maintained in winter, and the Forest Service strongly discourages travel on it from November to April. Commercial trucks are not allowed on the parkway, where the limit is 45 mph.
